proof_checks.reasoning: L is the continuous image of the compact and connected group U(2) x U(2). Therefore, L is compact (hence closed in the finite-dimensional space) and connected. Conjugation by the unitary V_t is a homeomorphism, preserving both topological properties.

Because V_t^dagger fixes the reference markers |00> and |01>, the action of H_t on W_R is entirely determined by the action of L on those markers, which spans all unit vectors 'a' in E and all orthonormal bases (b_0, b_u) in R. The parameterization e_j = V_t(a \otimes b_j) is exact and exhaustive.

proof_checks.claim: The compactness contradiction for a greatest orbit under actual OUTPUT-SET inclusion, also in the connected sublanguage.
proof_checks.reasoning: A greatest sufficient orbit must contain all orbits O_{H_n}, hence the sequence of Hadamard-pair realizations W_n. Because the orbit of a compact group is compact (and thus closed), it must contain the limit point W_\infty. Since W_\infty is blind, the greatest orbit cannot be sufficient. This holds in the connected sublanguage because each H_n is connected. The proof correctly uses orbit inclusion, not subgroup inclusion, and distinguishes greatest from maximal.
